dedupe_keys.name: earthquake damage and recovery of high speed rail in sichuan province dynamic input output simulation

description: This study simulates how high-speed rail and the regional economy recover after earthquakes in Sichuan Province, China. Junyi Wu and Taku Ishiro of Yokohama National University used a dynamic input-output model in which the high-speed rail transport sector is damaged and then restored alongside other industries, for earthquakes of different magnitudes, and traced effects on Sichuan, its neighbouring provinces and the whole of China, against the background of post-earthquake reconstruction in the province. They find that the recovery speed of the rail sector depends on the set restoration time and on the pace of recovery of adjacent industrial sectors and external inputs; faster recovery of those sectors speeds rail recovery, and once they return to normal the rail sector follows. Provinces with smaller economies, and provinces where high-speed rail is a large share of the economy, suffer larger relative economic losses. Coverage: Sichuan and China, stylised earthquake scenarios. Access: open-access article in the Journal of Economic Structures, 2024. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: sector-level economic modelling without physical network or damage simulation, and assumed restoration times. It supports resilience and cascading economic impact studies of rail recovery. It relates to the China high-speed railway operation data and the Asian international input-output tables in the catalogue.
